_comment: Everything the page says about THIS atlas. The viewer is generic; swap this file and the dataset and you have a different atlas. Inline markup: **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ==present-day highlight==. Era presets: the axis is a symmetric log around the CENTRE of from..to, so put the centre where the detail should be (usually the fork cluster around 2000) and let the edges be wide. 'sides' names the two halves of the canvas; each archetype picks its half with group.side in its part file.
title: Where We Are Now - a converging timeline of science fiction
headline: Every one of these histories
lede: Twenty-four science-fiction worlds, each pinned to the **real calendar** rather than its own. Every one of them rode along our history, broke away at one dated moment, and is drawn right up to the line where ==we are now==. Grouped by **how** they break with us rather than by genre - because that is what decides whether a world is hiding underneath this one, downstream of a war we won, or waiting ten thousand years ahead.
futureLabel: the future →   the years none of us have reached
legendHint: drag to pan · scroll to zoom · click a branch or card to enter that world

distribution.title: Where the charted time actually sits
distribution.blurb: Each world's recorded events, bucketed by when they land on the real calendar. The vertical rule is today: bars starting to its left are stories that begin in our past, and a long right tail means the fiction runs deep into the future.

worlds.title: Enter a world
worlds.blurb: Every card opens the full dossier: what the place is like to live in, who holds power, what the technology does and conspicuously refuses to do, where to begin, and which other worlds it genuinely connects to.

notes.heading: How this was built, and what to distrust
paragraphs: **The conversion problem.** Only some of these fictions date themselves in real years. Star Trek does - first contact is 5 April 2063. Everything else had to be converted: Star Wars counts from the Battle of Yavin, Dune counts After Guild, Foundation counts Galactic Era, Warhammer counts millennia. Read those positions as *projections*, not recorded history. Every event keeps its original in-universe label so you can check the arithmetic yourself.

**Star Wars really does land in the deep past.** Its own opening says "a long time ago", and converting BBY against a 1977 anchor puts the founding of the Republic around 23,000 BCE. That is not a sign error, and every world carries an *epoch* field saying which way it faces.

**The axis is warped.** The dataset runs from roughly 2 billion BCE to 48,000 CE, so the scale is a symmetric log: it stretches the centuries around now and compresses deep time, staying continuous and monotonic throughout. Year labels are exact; spacing is not. *Full reach* is the widest honest window.

**Confidence is recorded per event.** High means the fiction states it outright; medium means it was inferred or computed from a stated anchor; low means sources genuinely conflict - usually a book-versus-film or canon-level disagreement - and the competing claim is written out in the event note rather than quietly resolved.

**Editing it.** The dataset lives beside this file: one JSON file per archetype under `data/parts/`, world dossiers under `data/parts/worlds/`, the page copy in `data/atlas.json`, and the contract in `data/SCHEMA.md`. Run `python3 build-data.py` to validate and rebuild; it refuses to build on bad data, assembles the viewer from `src/`, and embeds the result here.
